EKF-SLAM with range-bearing landmarks

Source: R/ukf-slam.R
robot_ekf_slam.Rd

Simultaneous localization and mapping with an extended Kalman filter over the joint state \((x, y, \theta, m_{1x}, m_{1y}, \dots)\), with known data association: each measurement carries a landmark id. robot_ekf_slam() starts with the pose only. ekf_slam_predict() moves the pose with the exact unicycle model and its analytic Jacobians, updating the pose block and the pose-landmark cross covariances. ekf_slam_update() initializes a landmark the first time its id is seen with a positive range (a nonpositive first range is skipped with a warning, since the inverse model would place the landmark behind its bearing), from the inverse measurement model with the covariance \(G_x P_{xx} G_x^\top + G_z R G_z^\top\) and cross terms \(G_x P_{x\cdot}\), and fuses later sightings with a Joseph-form EKF update (Thrun, Burgard and Fox, 2005, chapter 10). The update costs time quadratic in the state size; an update that removes almost all of some variance (posterior below \(10^{-6}\) of the prior) is redone in factored form, which costs cubic time but keeps the small posterior accurate. ekf_slam_landmarks() returns the current map.

Usage

robot_ekf_slam(mean, cov, Q, R)

ekf_slam_predict(filter, control, dt)

ekf_slam_update(filter, measurements)

ekf_slam_landmarks(filter)

Arguments

mean

Initial pose estimate.

cov

Initial 3 by 3 pose covariance.

Q

Control noise covariance (2 by 2) on c(v, omega).

R

Measurement noise covariance (2 by 2, range then bearing, positive definite).

filter

A robot_ekf_slam.

control

c(v, omega).

dt

Duration (s).

measurements

A data frame with columns id, range, bearing, as returned by landmark_measurements().

Value

A robot_ekf_slam with mean, cov, ids (landmark ids in state order) and nis; ekf_slam_landmarks() returns a matrix of landmark estimates with ids as row names.

Examples

L <- rbind(a = c(2, 0), b = c(0, 2))
f <- robot_ekf_slam(c(0, 0, 0), diag(1e-6, 3), Q = diag(c(0.01, 0.01)),
                    R = diag(c(0.01, 0.001)))
f <- ekf_slam_update(f, landmark_measurements(c(0, 0, 0), L))
f <- ekf_slam_predict(f, c(1, 0), 0.5)
f <- ekf_slam_update(f, landmark_measurements(c(0.5, 0, 0), L))
ekf_slam_landmarks(f)
#>              x y
#> a 2.000000e+00 0
#> b 1.224647e-16 2
